CVE-2019-19699.topic: Authenticated code execution and privilege escalation
CVE-2019-19699.summary: The Centreon research follows a path through poller configuration and scheduled-task permissions. Administrative web access can lead to code execution, with a writable file used by a root cron task extending the impact.

CVE-2020-5844.topic: Authenticated file upload and code execution
CVE-2020-5844.summary: The proof of concept examines Pandora FMS’s administrator file repository. An uploaded PHP file can be executed through the application, turning administrative web access into code execution on the server.

CVE-2019-19369.summary: The original research documents how an authenticated user can use FusionPBX’s PHP editor to alter an existing server-side page. Visiting the altered page executes the inserted code with the web server’s permissions.

CVE-2019-19268.summary: Research by TheCyberGeek and dmw0ng into overly broad sudo permissions in rConfig. The original publication demonstrates several ways that the apache account can use permitted system utilities to act as root.

CVE-2019-16405.summary: The original publication links to TheCyberGeek’s Ruby proof of concept for Centreon. The CVE record also collects vendor fixes and release notes for affected Centreon versions.
